aliases: Background Imaging of Cosmic Extragalactic Polarization

facility_roles.quote: BICEP1 observed from the Amundsen-Scott South Pole Station between 2006 and 2008, mapping about 2% of the sky chosen to be uniquely clean of polarized foreground emission.

intervals.label: observations
intervals.note: The 2010 BICEP paper says "During three seasons of observing at the South Pole (2006 through 2008)"; the end is recorded at year precision (the last observing month is not stated).
intervals.quote: BICEP has completed 3 years of successful observations at the South Pole beginning in 2006 February.

intervals.label: observations ended
intervals.note: No source states a decommissioning date; BICEP1 "observed ... between 2006 and 2008" (LAMBDA), "three seasons of observations at the South Pole (2006 to 2008)" (arXiv:1310.1422), so completion is recorded at year precision, 2008.
intervals.quote: During three seasons of observing at the South Pole (2006 through 2008)

name: BICEP1
notes: No INSPIRE experiment id is recorded: INSPIRE was not contacted by this stream.
The BICEP2 paper states the full three-year BICEP1 data set "yields the best direct limits to date on inflationary B-modes: r < 0.65 at 95% confidence level".

physics_goals.quote: Background Imaging of Cosmic Extragalactic Polarization (BICEP) is a bolometric polarimeter designed to measure the inflationary B-mode polarization of the cosmic microwave background (CMB) at degree angular scales.
physics_goals.value: Measure the inflationary B-mode polarization of the CMB at degree angular scales.

summary.plain: The first BICEP telescope: a small refractor at the South Pole that spent three years (2006-2008) mapping a clean 2% of the sky in polarization, looking for the imprint of gravitational waves from inflation.
summary.technical: Bolometric CMB polarimeter at the South Pole (Dark Sector Laboratory) observing 2006-2008 at 100 and 150 GHz; direct B-mode limit r < 0.65 (95%) from the three-year data set; pathfinder for BICEP2 and the Keck Array.
